checks.quote: Our Master's Program at Cal State LA offers a comprehensive education in the rapidly changing and emerging field of Computer Science and prepares students to enter the competitive technology industry.
With the approval of the CS advisor, choose 18 units of 4000/5000 level courses as well as the Thesis and Project courses.
Complete 24 units of 4000/5000 level courses and undertake a comprehensive examination to demonstrate your knowledge.

Anyone with a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a closely related field with an overall GPA of 3.0 may apply. Prerequisite courses may be required for non-CS students or for students from non-ABET accredited CS programs.
GRE and Recommendation letters are NOT required
Promising applicants with a GPA between 2.5 and 2.99 may be conditionally admitted and are encouraged to apply
Applicants must possess a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a closely related field with an overall GPA of 3.0 or better to be considered for full admission
A promising applicant with a GPA between 2.5 and 2.99 may be conditionally admitted as a special action student.
These students are given up to three prerequisites (based on the evaluation of their transcripts).
The application process is centralized at the university and requires TWO steps as described below:
The MS CS degree requires the completion of 30 units.
The minimum requirement for candidacy advancement are the completion of 12 units and a minimum GPA of 3.0.
CS 5990 should be taken exactly twice.
The Graduate Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) is no longer required for graduate students, effective for catalog years beginning Fall 2023.
Spring 2027 classes begin January 25, 2027.
Fall 2027 classes begin August 23, 2027.

My research focuses on Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Data Science for various applications including sustainability, environment (wildfire, air quality), healthcare, traffic management, and other social good applications.

My research explores AI for computational biology, health informatics, and human-computer interaction, with a focus on augmenting human capabilities and decision-making.
